title: Meadow vs Treez: 2026 Dispensary POS Comparison
summary: Meadow vs Treez compared for 2026: daily speed, delivery, Metrc compliance, hardware, support, and total cost, plus what operators who ran both platforms chose.
body_markdown:
Meadow and Treez are built for different kinds of operations. Treez is enterprise-positioned for large multi-state operators, with reporting depth, an open API, and modular products billed separately. Meadow is an all-in-one platform that runs single stores and multi-location chains alike, with POS, ecommerce, delivery, inventory, and Metrc compliance in a single system and a single bill.


**The short answer: if you have an IT department, Treez fits. If you need your team to learn the system today, Meadow is simpler and faster. This guide compares the two on daily speed, delivery, compliance, support, and total cost, using verified G2 reviews and the accounts of operators who have run both.**

**Key Takeaways**


- **Treez holds a[3.3 out of 5 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/treez/reviews)** , with recurring critical themes around platform reliability, reporting gaps, and support responsiveness. **Meadow holds 4.9 out of 5 from more than 90 verified reviews and is the[#1 rated cannabis POS on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/meadow-meadow/reviews) .**
- Treez delivery is state-specific and requires a support request to enable, and operators typically extend it with a route-planning integration such as Cannveya or Onfleet. Meadow delivery is native to the POS, including hub-and-spoke and dynamic models.
- Treez runs on Windows hardware. Meadow runs on iPad, which matters most at switchover: Three Greens Collective described the move to Windows as expensive and driver-heavy, and the move back to Meadow as plug and play.
- Two California operators have run both systems and chosen Meadow. Three Greens Collective in Calexico left Meadow for Treez and was back on Meadow in two to three days. Xzibit's West Coast Collective ran Meadow at one store and Treez at two, then standardized on Meadow.
- Treez bills POS, ecommerce, and delivery as separate products. Meadow bundles them into the plan, and publishes exactly what each plan includes on the[pricing page](https://getmeadow.com/pricing) before you request a quote.
- Treez is built for large multi-state operators, but store count alone should not decide this. Off the Charts opened more than 30 California locations in two years on Meadow and now runs more than 40. The question underneath it is how much configuration work your team wants to own.

## Three Questions to Answer Before You Compare Platforms


The fastest way to narrow a POS shortlist is to describe how your team actually works, then check which platform matches. Three questions do most of that work.


**1. How many systems do you log into to run one promotion?** If the answer is three or more, you are losing time to context switching every time you run a same-day deal. Ask each vendor to show you the full path from discount setup to live online menu, timed, on a real store.


**2. How long does it take a new budtender to ring their first sale alone?** If it takes more than a shift, training cost is compounding against your turnover rate. Ask what training the vendor requires before a new hire can work the register, and whether that training is self-paced or scheduled.


**3. Do you run delivery, or plan to in the next twelve months?** If yes, ask whether delivery is built into the POS or enabled as a separate feature, what it costs, and whether route planning requires a third vendor. The answer changes both your monthly bill and the number of people you call when something breaks at 9pm.


Your answers narrow the field faster than any feature list. The sections below fill in the detail behind each one.

## What Operators Say About Treez


Treez holds a[3.3 out of 5 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/treez/reviews) , and the recurring themes in critical reviews are platform reliability, reporting and analytics gaps, and support responsiveness. Treez is a real platform with a real customer base, particularly among multi-state operators in California, and its open API model is a genuine strength for teams that want to build their own stack.


Two verified reviews, quoted as written:


> **They have poor reporting, updates to the platform often break other things.**
>
>
> Chelsea S., verified review collected by and hosted on G2.com


> **Right now, Treez seems to the main source of our problems as a whole for our retail group.**
>
>
> Verified review collected by and hosted on G2.com


Reviews are one input, not a verdict. Weigh them against what your own operation needs, and ask Treez directly about anything that concerns you. An enterprise retail group with an internal IT function experiences a configuration-heavy platform very differently than a three-store operator whose general manager is also the system administrator.

## Five Tasks to Time on Both Systems


The most reliable way to compare two POS platforms is to time the same five tasks on each during a demo, with a stopwatch, rather than reading a feature grid. Ask both vendors to run these live.


Time this exact moment on both systems. Checkout speed is the task operators underestimate most.


**Add a flash sale to your online menu.** In Meadow, discounts and the online menu live in one system, so a same-day promo is set once and pushed live. In Treez, ecommerce runs through Treez Ecommerce, a separate retailer-facing storefront product, so ask how the discount propagates and how you verify the two are synced. If you run weekly promos, that gap compounds. For the underlying strategy, see[how to build a profitable dispensary discount strategy](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dispensary-discount-strategy) .


**Train a new budtender to ring a sale alone.** Ask each vendor what a new hire has to complete before working the register unsupervised, and whether that training is self-paced. Then ask to watch someone do it.


**Close out at end of night.** Ask where closeout happens: inside the register flow on the same device, or in a separate back-office module on separate hardware. Time it both ways.


**Find a specific package in Metrc during a rush.** This is the task operators underestimate. Ask each vendor to search for a package by partial tag, mid-transaction, on the register. For how this works day to day, see our guide to[Metrc reporting for dispensaries](https://getmeadow.com/blog/metrc-reporting-for-dispensaries) , or read more about[Meadow's Metrc compliance](https://getmeadow.com/features/metrc-compliance) .


**Get help when something breaks.** Ask what happens at 7pm on a Saturday. Meadow's support chat provides live agent responses in under five minutes. Ask Treez for their equivalent response-time commitment in writing.


If three or more of these are painful on your current system today, the problem is structural, and a feature comparison will not fix it.

## Two Operators Who Ran Both Systems


Two California retailers have run Meadow and Treez and published what happened, which is more useful than any vendor claim.


**Three Greens Collective** , Calexico, CA, ran Meadow from 2021, switched to Treez on the promise of new features, and found those features were still in beta or not yet built. Creative Director Oscar Valles described two problems that followed.


The first was hardware. Moving from Meadow's iPad-based software to Windows meant existing equipment was not compatible due to driver settings, and Valles configured every computer, scanner, receipt printer, and register individually.


The second was compliance:


> **We also experienced difficulty with the Treez METRC integration and keeping our business compliant. The point of sale system didn't meet our needs. We missed the simplicity of using Meadow and wished we had never switched.**
>
>
> Oscar Valles, Creative Director, Three Greens Collective


Coming back took two to three days, and because the iPad hardware was still on the shelf, Valles described the setup as plug and play.[Read the full switchback Q&A](https://getmeadow.com/blog/the-pos-switchover-why-choosing-the-right-cannabis-retail-software-matters) .


**West Coast Collective** , founded by Xzibit, ran the cleanest comparison available: one location on Meadow, two on Treez, with the same staff floating between all three. The budtenders and managers using both systems every day chose Meadow for all three stores. The migration ran overnight, with hardware installed the night before and a Metrc cleanup completed in advance.[Read the West Coast Collective case study](https://getmeadow.com/blog/how-xzibits-west-coast-collective-made-the-switch-to-meadow-without-missing) .


The pattern in both accounts is the same. Treez gives you levers to pull, and someone on your payroll has to pull them.


West Coast Collective ran one store on Meadow and two on Treez. The staff using both chose Meadow.

## What to Ask About Total Cost


Comparing sticker prices on two cannabis POS platforms will mislead you, because the platforms bundle differently. The only comparison that holds up is total annual cost for your actual configuration, which means asking both vendors the same four questions and getting the answers in writing.


**What is billed separately from the core POS fee?** Treez ecommerce runs through Treez Ecommerce, a separate product. Ask whether delivery, ecommerce, loyalty, and reporting are included or line items. Meadow lists what each plan contains on the[pricing page](https://getmeadow.com/pricing) , so you can see the bundling before anyone quotes you.


**What does delivery actually require?** If route planning needs Cannveya or Onfleet, that vendor's fee belongs in your total. Meadow's delivery is native, and higher-volume licenses can optionally add a two-way Onfleet integration. See[how Meadow handles delivery](https://getmeadow.com/features/cannabis-delivery) .


**What is the hardware cost, including what you already own?** This is where Three Greens got hit. Ask specifically whether your current scanners, printers, and registers are compatible, and who does the configuration.


**What is the three-year total, including every add-on?** Ask for it before you accept a renewal discount. Then set it beside a single bill.


Both platforms quote custom, so the fair comparison is not the sticker price, it is how many line items sit underneath it. Ask both vendors to put the full bundle in writing.


**If you are paying three vendors to do one job, it is worth seeing the alternative side by side.** Meadow will walk your actual configuration and give you transparent pricing on the first call.[Book a Call to Learn More](https://getmeadow.com/schedule-demo)

## When Meadow Is the Better Fit


Meadow is the better choice for operators who want the platform to absorb the operational work rather than hand it to their team. Three conditions make that concrete.


**Delivery is part of the business, now or soon.** Meadow builds hub-and-spoke and dynamic delivery into the POS, with an optional two-way Onfleet integration for higher-volume licenses. Treez delivery is state-specific, requires a support request to enable, and is typically extended with a route-planning vendor. If delivery is a real line of your revenue, that is the difference between one system and three. See[how Meadow handles delivery](https://getmeadow.com/features/cannabis-delivery) .


**Nobody on your payroll administers the POS full time.** This is the pattern in both switchback accounts above. Treez gives you levers, and someone has to pull them. If your general manager is also your system administrator, configuration overhead comes directly out of floor time. Off the Charts opened stores in as little as a week on Meadow, and reached 40-plus locations, without staffing an internal platform team to do it.


**You want one bill instead of three.** Meadow's ecommerce and delivery are part of the plan rather than separate subscriptions, and the[pricing page](https://getmeadow.com/pricing) lists what each tier includes before you talk to anyone. Treez bills ecommerce and delivery as separate products. If you are building a multi-store pro forma, one bundled line is easier to model than a base fee plus add-ons that scale differently.


---


## When Treez Is the Better Fit


Treez is the better choice for operators whose requirements sit outside Meadow's footprint or above its intended scale. Three cases stand out.


**State coverage.** Treez operates in more states. Meadow serves California, New York, New Jersey, Michigan, Massachusetts, and Minnesota.


**Reporting and API depth for teams that build their own stack.** Treez is built around reporting depth and an open API, and it is positioned squarely at large multi-state operators. A group with analysts and developers on staff can extend that architecture in ways a platform with a fixed feature set will not match. Store count alone will not settle it, though. What settles it is whether you have people whose job is to maintain the system.


What to look for in a long-term partner is the same regardless of which way you go: ask who you call when the register is down, ask what happens when you request a feature, and ask two current customers at your size what they would change.

## Common Questions


### What is the difference between Meadow and Treez?


Meadow is an all-in-one platform with POS, ecommerce, delivery, inventory, and Metrc compliance in one system and one bill, serving single stores through 40-plus location chains. Treez is enterprise-positioned, with reporting depth, an open API, and ecommerce and delivery handled as separate products. Meadow runs on iOS; Treez runs on Windows.


### Can I switch from Treez to Meadow?


Yes. Three Greens Collective was live again on Meadow in two to three days, and West Coast Collective migrated three locations overnight. Timeline depends on the size of your operation and the state of your Metrc account, which Meadow's implementation team audits before migration day.


### Will switching from Treez trigger a Metrc audit?


No. Meadow migrates historical sales with package IDs intact and files the same reports automatically, so your compliance record is continuous. Meadow helps operators stay compliant and does not provide legal advice; confirm anything state-specific with your regulator or compliance counsel.


### How does Treez compare to Meadow on transaction speed?


The architectures differ in ways that show up at the register. Meadow runs closeout and Metrc package lookup inside the same iPad flow as the sale. Treez separates ecommerce into its own product and runs on Windows hardware. Time both on the same five tasks during your demos rather than relying on either vendor's claim.


### Does Treez have native delivery?


Treez offers limited native delivery functionality that is state-specific and requires a support request to enable, and operators typically extend it with a route-planning integration such as Cannveya or Onfleet. Meadow includes hub-and-spoke and dynamic delivery natively in the POS, with an optional two-way Onfleet integration for higher-volume licenses.


### What is Meadow's uptime?


Meadow has maintained 99.99% uptime since 2014, including 100% uptime on every 4/20 since 2015.
